repo.description:
## Summary

SurrealDB's Surrealism WASM plugin runtime builds the outbound network allowlist for guest WASI Preview 2 sockets from a module's declared `allow_net` entries without ever re-checking the resolved IP addresses against the server's `deny_net` policy or against private, loopback, and link-local ranges. An authenticated principal who can load and invoke a Surrealism module (with the experimental `surrealism` capability enabled) can declare `allow_net = ["attacker-controlled-hostname"]` whose DNS record points at a forbidden address such as a cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), a loopback service (127.0.0.1), or an RFC1918 host. Load-time validation inspects the entry only as a host string and admits it; the runtime then resolves the hostname and stores the resulting private or denied IP directly in the guest socket filter, so guest WASM can open a raw TCP or UDP connection to an operator-forbidden internal endpoint. This is server-side request forgery over arbitrary TCP and UDP protocols and ports, defeating the exact `deny_net` egress guard that several prior SurrealDB SSRF advisories were published to enforce.

## Root Cause

SurrealDB enforces outbound network policy through an allow-list combined with a deny-list (`Capabilities::allows_network_target` = `allow_net.matches(target) && !deny_net.matches(target)`). For the reqwest-based HTTP and JWKS clients this policy is completed at DNS time by `FilteringResolver`, which re-checks each resolved IP against the deny-list and private-IP ranges. The Surrealism raw-socket path has no equivalent re-check, and load-time validation compares only host strings, so a hostname that resolves to a denied or private IP is never blocked.

Two independent gaps combine:

1. Load-time validation is string-only. `validate_surrealism_capabilities` checks each `allow_net` entry via `NetTarget::from_str` and `allows_network_target`. An IP-range `deny_net` entry is a `NetTarget::IPNet`; matching it against a domain target (`NetTarget::Host(Domain)`) falls through to the `_ => false` arm of `NetTarget::matches`, so the deny-list never matches a hostname. A literal-IP `allow_net` entry would be rejected here, but a hostname is admitted.
2. Runtime resolution has no deny or private-IP filter. `resolve_allow_net` resolves the admitted hostname to its IP and stores `ResolvedNetAllow::Net(<resolved IP>)` (portless entries match on any port). The WASI socket gate installed by `wasi_context::build` (`socket_addr_check`) admits an outbound connection whenever any allow filter matches the destination, with no consultation of `deny_net` or private-IP ranges.

```text
Affected components (repository-relative paths):
- surrealism/runtime/src/net_allow.rs
    resolve_allow_net / resolve_hostname (lines 46-107): resolves module allow_net
    hostnames to IPs and stores them for the WASI allowlist with no deny/private filter;
    ResolvedNetAllow::matches_socket_addr (lines 20-27) is allow-only and ignores port.
- surrealism/runtime/src/wasi_context.rs
    build (lines 114-155): installs socket_addr_check (lines 137-146) that admits any
    outbound connect matching an allow filter, with no deny_net/private-IP gate, and
    leaves TCP/UDP enabled for a non-empty allowlist.
- surrealdb/core/src/dbs/capabilities.rs
    validate_surrealism_capabilities (lines 1006-1057): string-only load check;
    NetTarget::matches (lines 261-284) returns false for an IPNet deny entry against a
    Host(Domain) target, so a hostname resolving to a denied IP passes.
```

## Impact

An attacker who can load and invoke a Surrealism module against a server with the experimental `surrealism` capability enabled can cause the server to open raw TCP and UDP connections to endpoints the operator explicitly forbade through `deny_net`. Prerequisites: the experimental `surrealism` capability is enabled; the attacker is authenticated with enough privilege to upload a `.surli` module to a bucket and invoke it; and the operator relies on `deny_net` (with a broad or attacker-influenceable `allow_net`) for egress control, which is the same threat model the prior SSRF advisories address. Given those conditions, exploitation is deterministic and requires no user interaction.

The demonstrated capability is full outbound reach to internal, loopback, and cloud-metadata addresses over arbitrary TCP and UDP ports, with responses returnable to the attacker through the module return value or the module KV store. This enables reading cloud instance metadata (for example IAM credentials at 169.254.169.254), reaching internal-only services, and sending arbitrary bytes to internal TCP and UDP listeners. The reqwest-mediated module surface (`http::*`, `sql()`, `run()`) does honor `deny_net`, so the raw-socket path is a silent inconsistency the operator cannot anticipate rather than a documented capability of module loading.

## Proof of Concept

`Requires a server started with the experimental surrealism capability enabled, a broad allow_net (for example allow_net = all) plus a deny_net covering private/metadata ranges, and a principal able to upload and invoke a module. The vulnerable runtime predicate can also be exercised directly against surrealism/runtime.`

Reproduction outline:

1. Register a hostname (for example `internal.attacker.example`) with a DNS A record pointing at a denied address such as `169.254.169.254` (or use `localhost`, which resolves to `127.0.0.1`).
2. Build a `.surli` module whose `surrealism.toml` declares `allow_net = ["internal.attacker.example"]` and whose guest code opens a WASI outbound TCP socket to that host on an attacker-chosen port, reads the response, and returns it.
3. Upload and invoke the module. Load-time validation admits the hostname; the runtime resolves it to the denied IP and installs it in the guest socket allowlist; the guest connects and exfiltrates the response.

The runtime predicate that makes this succeed is directly observable in source (`surrealism/runtime/src/net_allow.rs`):

```text
resolve_allow_net(["localhost"]) -> [ResolvedNetAllow::Net(127.0.0.1/32)]
ResolvedNetAllow::Net(127.0.0.1/32).matches_socket_addr(127.0.0.1:6379) == true
ResolvedNetAllow::Net(127.0.0.1/32).matches_socket_addr(127.0.0.1:8080) == true   (any port)
```

A literal-IP entry (`allow_net = ["127.0.0.1"]`) is instead rejected at load, confirming the hostname indirection is necessary and sufficient.

## Attack Chain

1. **Exposure:** A principal authorized to load and invoke Surrealism modules reaches `Context::get_surrealism_module` (surrealdb/core/src/ctx/context.rs:1259), which is gated behind the experimental `surrealism` capability. The module bytes are supplied by the attacker as a `.surli` archive.
2. **Control:** The attacker fully controls the module's `surrealism.toml`, including `allow_net`, and controls the DNS record for the hostname it lists.
3. **Path:** `validate_surrealism_capabilities` (surrealdb/core/src/dbs/capabilities.rs:1044-1053) checks each `allow_net` entry only as a string. With a broad `allow_net`, the allow side matches; the `deny_net` IPNet entries do not match the domain target because `NetTarget::matches` returns false for an IPNet-versus-Host(Domain) comparison (capabilities.rs:277-281), so the hostname passes.
4. **Path:** `Runtime::new` calls `resolve_allow_net` (surrealism/runtime/src/net_allow.rs:46-107), which resolves the hostname to the denied IP and stores `ResolvedNetAllow::Net(<denied IP>)` for the guest socket filter.
5. **Guard:** None on the raw-socket path. `wasi_context::build` installs `socket_addr_check` (surrealism/runtime/src/wasi_context.rs:137-146) that admits an outbound connect when any allow filter matches, with no `deny_net` or private-IP check; portless entries match on any port. Disabling guest DNS (`allow_ip_name_lookup(false)`) does not help, because the guest connects to the resolved IP literal already installed in the filter.
6. **Primitive:** The guest opens a raw WASI Preview 2 TCP or UDP socket to the denied internal, loopback, or metadata endpoint.
7. **Result:** Server-side request forgery to an operator-forbidden endpoint over arbitrary TCP and UDP ports, with responses exfiltrated through the module return value or KV store.

## Bypass Evidence

The prior SurrealDB deny-net and SSRF fixes are the relevant existing protection, and they do not cover this path. `FilteringResolver` (surrealdb/core/src/net/mod.rs:69-142) is a `reqwest::dns::Resolve` implementation that re-checks resolved IPs against `deny_net` and private ranges. It is wired at exactly two sites: the general HTTP client (surrealdb/core/src/http/mod.rs:94) and the JWKS client (surrealdb/core/src/iam/jwks.rs:353). Both are reqwest clients. The Surrealism guest uses WASI Preview 2 sockets, which never route through reqwest, so `FilteringResolver` cannot run for them.

Disproof attempts performed and their outcomes:

- Searched the entire `surrealism/runtime` crate for any `deny_net` or `is_private` reference on the resolve or socket path: zero matches. No re-check exists on this path.
- Checked for a second load-time pass that resolves the hostname and re-checks IPs (a `NetTarget::resolve` helper exists in the core capabilities module): it is not called from `validate_surrealism_capabilities` or from the Surrealism load path.
- Confirmed the module's own HTTP surface (`http::*`, `sql()`, `run()`) is correctly guarded via a deny_net-backed client, so the vulnerability is specific to the raw-socket path and is a genuine, unanticipated inconsistency rather than a documented consequence of module loading.
- Confirmed a literal-IP `allow_net` entry is rejected at load, so this is not simply "the operator allowed the IP"; only the hostname indirection defeats the guard.
- Verified the latest published prerelease still ships the unfixed code (see Affected Versions), ruling out an already-released fix.

No prior published advisory references Surrealism or WASI sockets; a search of the repository advisory set for those terms returns no matches. This is a distinct, unfixed vector rather than a duplicate of any prior fix.

## Affected Versions

- `Ecosystem: rust (crates.io)`
- `Package: surrealdb-core (default-on "surrealism" feature, pulling surrealism-runtime), shipped in the surreal server binary`
- `Confirmed affected range: >= 3.1.0`
- `Latest release checked: surrealdb-core 3.2.4 (latest stable) and 3.3.0-beta.4 (latest prerelease) on crates.io; latest prerelease pulls surrealism-runtime 0.6.0-beta.4`
- `Fix status: not fixed in any released version`

The Surrealism WASI socket path did not exist at 3.0.0 (the file is absent) and first appears at 3.1.0. The `surrealism/runtime/src/net_allow.rs` artifact is byte-identical (git blob 39ffd9b1a4f1ff79bbf46d4076698db46386bd99) across tags v3.1.0, v3.2.4, and v3.3.0-beta.3, matches the reviewed source revision, and is unchanged in the surrealism-runtime 0.6.0-beta.4 crate downloaded from the registry (which surrealdb-core 3.3.0-beta.4 depends on). The `wasi_context.rs` socket gate is likewise allow-only in that latest published crate, and the runtime crate contains no `deny_net` or private-IP reference. Because no released version contains a fix and the boundary is open-ended, the range is expressed as `>= 3.1.0` with no upper bound. Note on coordinate: the vulnerable code physically lives in the separately versioned crate surrealism-runtime, reached only through surrealdb-core's default-on "surrealism" feature; the 3.x range reflects the surrealdb-core and server artifact that operators actually install.

## Suggested Fix

Enforce the resolved-IP egress policy on the Surrealism raw-socket path so it matches the reqwest path. When `resolve_allow_net` resolves a hostname to one or more IPs, each resolved IP must be re-checked against the server `deny_net` policy and against private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges before it is admitted to the guest socket allowlist; resolved addresses that violate the policy must be dropped or the load rejected. Equivalently, make the `socket_addr_check` filter in `wasi_context::build` deny-aware by threading the server `deny_net` and a private-IP predicate into it, mirroring the `FilteringResolver` semantics. The remediation must cover both TCP and UDP, portless (any-port) entries, IPv4 and IPv6 including IPv4-mapped IPv6, and the case where `allow_net` is broad (for example set to all) so that `deny_net` remains the operative guard.

Interim mitigation without a code change: do not enable the experimental `surrealism` capability on servers that rely on `deny_net` for egress isolation; restrict who may upload and invoke modules; and enforce egress restrictions at the network or firewall layer (for example blocking access to 169.254.169.254 and internal ranges from the database host) rather than relying solely on `deny_net`.

---

Reported by zx (GitHub: @manus-pi).

### Patches

A patch has been created in the Surrealism runtime that applies operator `--deny-net` rules to the module socket allowlist and rejects a resolved private or special-use address, closing the SSRF path via a hostname that resolves to a private IP. The enforcement was introduced as part of the Surrealism networking rework; there is no dedicated single-commit fix.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealDB Documentation - Capabilities](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealdb/security/capabilities)
- `Lend Surrealism a transaction handle and make async real` (commit `0fc51a0bad`)
